key_insight: Solution precursor plasma spraying can directly produce porous, disordered Ni–Fe–Al oxide anodes whose aluminum-driven amorphization boosts oxygen-evolution performance and durability.
engineering_relevance: The process offers a scalable, platinum-group-metal-free route to high-activity water-electrolysis anodes that better bridge lab catalyst design and industrial coating production.
method: Solution precursor plasma spraying used to fabricate Ni–Fe–Al oxide coatings
Aluminum added to suppress crystal growth and promote amorphous, porous microstructures
Mild post-annealing at 300°C tested for adhesion and stability
evidence_signal: The coated anodes reached 0.5 A cm−2 at 1.74 V vs RHE and sustained operation for 160 h in 1 M KOH, with a reported degradation rate of 150 µV h−1 after recovery.
watch_item: Initial 300°C annealing lowers OER activity before recovery, so coating optimization must balance adhesion benefits against short-term performance loss.
paper_title: Scalable Production of Disordered Nickel‐Iron‐Aluminum Oxides as Stable Anodes for Water Electrolysis: The Role of Aluminum
